title: Quantization regression workshop - KV aging, batching, and VPC constraints
summary: Deep technical triage of a post-quantize accuracy regression observed on Aurelia's internal clinical summarization workload. Focus areas: INT8/AWQ vs FP8 behavior, GPTQ layer sensitivity, KV cache staleness and affinity, batching-induced tokenization edge-cases, and constraints from VPC/on-prem networking. Agreed to run targeted bisect with layer probes, share benchmark artifacts and security checklist; Redwood to provide a canary config and a small script to replay failing seeds in a private VPC test cluster.
topics: accuracy regression symptoms and hypothesis prioritization
quant formats compared: INT8, GPTQ, AWQ, FP8
KV cache staleness and sticky affinity behavior
batching windows, tokenization mismatches, and cold cache effects
VPC networking constraints for on-prem pilot and replay tooling
action_items: Samira: produce layer-probe script (python) and share on slack — due 2026-06-02
Marcus: extract 50 failing prompts + seeds and upload benchmark.csv to shared drive — due 2026-06-01
Priya: open firewall rules for the VPC test cluster and confirm egress to Redwood debug endpoints — due 2026-06-04
Jordan: send security checklist & preliminary canary config (dedicated + fallback to hosted) — due 2026-05-31
next_steps: Redwood to attach canary config and a short replay script in the CRM ticket
Customer to run probe script in on-prem staging with GPTQ and AWQ variants
Joint meeting next week to review bisect results and decide fallback policy
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-30 15:00 UTC | Duration 62m | Link: https://app.fireflies.ai/ff/ff-20260530-7843
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Jordan from Redwood, AE. Samira will lead the deep dive. Marcus, Priya, Leo, thanks for making time.
[00:08] Marcus: Yeah thanks, quick context — we rolled gptq-int8 hybrid last week into staging and saw a 6-7% drop on our ROUGE-like metric for clinical summarization. Not all prompts fail, it's... it's like a zipper, some clusters fail spectacularly.
[00:22] Samira: Right, thanks. So we'll try to run through symptoms, what we've seen in profiling, and then propose bisect steps. Quick q: you ran with KV cache warm, cold, or mixed?
[00:33] Marcus: Mixed. Most of the failing traces had been through user sessions with sticky affinity, so KV warm for some but we do observe cold-starts during bursts.
[00:45] Priya: Also want to flag the VPC egress constraints — our test cluster can't reach some of Redwood's debug endpoints unless we open those firewall rules. We're prepping that change now.
[00:55] Samira: OK noted. Two hypothesis we prioritize: layer-wise quant sensitivity (GPTQ rounding artifacts at specific layers) and KV cache staleness interacting with prefix caching when batch coalescing changes token offsets.
[01:10] Leo: Can you unpack the batching interaction? Our engineers think batching shouldn't change outputs, but we see diffs when concurrency increases.
[01:18] Samira: Yeah, usually it's deterministic, but the runtime does two things: it coalesces requests into a single attention pass and uses KV cache offsets to map positions. If tokenization or padding differs slightly between requests, the offsets end up mismatched and the runtime rewrites attention indices — small, but amplified in quantized inner products.
[01:34] Marcus: We did notice some prompts where length+tokenizer choice produced an extra sentinel token.
[01:40] Jordan: Note — tokenizer variances are a common gotcha. We pushed tokenizer sync flags recently but maybe your client is on an older pip package.
[01:50] Marcus: We're on internal forked tokenizer 0.9.6-custom. Might be a culprit.
[02:00] Samira: For the quant formats: empirically, GPQ/GP TQ — sorry GPTQ — tends to shift logits in the tails for a subset of heads. AWQ (adaptive weight quant) sometimes preserves top-k but introduces small bias on mid-range logits. FP8 tends to preserve distribution shape but costs more throughput. INT8 symmetric quant often yields better throughput but is brittle on certain layer norms.
[02:22] Marcus: So which to prioritize for bisect?
[02:26] Samira: Step 1: reproduce deterministically with seed+prompt replay. Step 2: run layer-probe where we run mixed-precision: swap single layers back to fp32 or fp16 and check delta. That narrows the suspect layers. Step 3: inspect KV interactions — run same seeds with fixed batching=1 (no coalescing) and with kernel-level debug logs.
[02:46] Leo: Is that safe on our VPC cluster? We want minimal network egress.
[02:51] Jordan: We can provide a small replay binary that runs fully inside your VPC; the only thing we'd need is a temporary signed artifact exchange. Priya, does that sound OK?
[03:01] Priya: Need to confirm with infra but yes, we prefer artifacts that run in-house.
[03:05] Samira: We'll also attach a layer-probe script that toggles quantized->fp at runtime per layer. It's lightweight — just load model, replace quant kernels for layer i, run the failing seeds.
[03:17] Marcus: Great. On the failing prompts we see seed sensitivity — some seeds fail only when cached kv is used from previous session. Could it be kv-staleness causing attention mismatch?
[03:29] Samira: Yes. If cached KV corresponds to different token offsets (due to pad/trim differences) the positional encoding applied at attention time shifts. In quantized math that shift can push a head over a threshold and cascade.
[03:42] Leo: Are there known pathologies in AWQ vs GPTQ here? We haven't tried AWQ fully.
[03:47] Samira: AWQ can be more robust for some models because it adjusts scale per weight-block, but it also introduces extra micro-bias per block. GPTQ's per-weight rounding can create rare high-magnitude outliers. So it's model and layer dependent.
[04:03] Marcus: Our initial test used GPTQ-int8 mix. Should we try AWQ-int8?
[04:08] Samira: Yes, try AWQ and also FP8 as a control. FP8 will be slower but should tell you whether quantization is the primary cause. If FP8 fixes it, then it's almost certainly quant-induced.
[04:18] Jordan: Also check our 'precision-fallback' runtime flag — it will re-route layers identified as unstable to a fallback kernel which keeps the rest quantized. That is what we usually recommend in production SLOs.
[04:30] Marcus: How much throughput do we lose with per-layer fallbacks?
[04:33] Samira: Depends on which layers are un-fallbacked. If it's 2 mid layers you're looking at 10-20% throughput regression for that model; if the whole head stack then more. But usually it's worth it for correctness.
[04:46] Priya: On networking: our staging is in an air-gapped-ish VPC — we can run the replay but we need the script plus the mirror of the model artifact. Can Redwood provide a signed S3 manifest or container we can pull?
[04:58] Jordan: Yes we can. We'll provide a tarball with model+probe; for on-prem we can also provide a minimal Docker image. We'll send the signed manifest via secure share.
[05:08] Marcus: You mentioned kernel selection — any chance the compilation/kernels changed between baseline and current production? We upgrade runtime last month.
[05:15] Samira: Good point — the kernel registry did pick a new attention kernel optimized for sequence length 1024. If your workload has many shorter sequences, kernel heuristics might select a path that interacts poorly with quantization. We'll cross-check runtime versions.
[05:28] Leo: Where in the logs do we see kernel selection? We couldn't find a clear marker.
[05:33] Samira: We'll enable verbose runtime logging for you. It writes a 'kernel_trace' block at load time with decisions per layer. We'll also include it in the probe.
[05:42] Marcus: Are there known tokenizer->batching edgecases that cause invisible char insertion? We've seen mysterious 0xE2 bytes in a few runs.
[05:50] Samira: That sounds like an encoding/normalization mismatch — different environments may apply normalization. Tokenizer versions, locale, or even differing unicode libs can cause those weird bytes. That can shift token alignment and then KV offsets. So sync tokenizer version exactly.
[06:03] Jordan: Action wise: Samira will drop the probe script today. Jordan will drop canary config and the security checklist. Marcus will gather failing seeds. Priya will open the firewall for the limited debug egress and confirm model pull paths.
[06:15] Marcus: For the bisect plan: after layer probe, if we identify suspect layers, do we want a canary on a small % of production traffic or run isolated staging?
[06:24] Samira: Start in staging in your VPC with canary replay. If the probe indicates 2-3 layers, run a sticky-canary (10% of sessions) with fallback enabled. We can also do A/B with AWQ vs GPTQ to compare user-visible metrics.
[06:38] Leo: Do you have a lightweight metric hook to compute our clinical-ROUGE in runtime so we can monitor regression in real-time?
[06:44] Jordan: We can share a small eval endpoint and a quick node/python client that computes a streaming delta and posts to your prometheus or an S3 CSV.
[06:52] Marcus: Perfect. One more thing — compliance/logging. We need to ensure key management for model artifacts and logs.
[06:58] Jordan: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS; logs can be configured to remain in your VPC. We'll include the compliance checklist in the doc bundle.
[07:09] Samira: Ok I'll summarize the technical bisect: 1) deterministic replay + seed set, 2) run probes with per-layer precision swap, 3) run with batching=1 vs batch-coalescing to isolate offset issues, 4) test AWQ and FP8 variants, 5) analyze kernel_trace and kv-timestamps.
[07:29] Marcus: Sounds good. How soon can we get the scripts?
[07:32] Samira: I'll post them to the CRM ticket and slack by EOD tomorrow. Jordan will pop the canary and security note now.
[07:39] Priya: I'll confirm firewall changes by Friday.
[07:42] Jordan: Great. Anything else?
[07:44] Marcus: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[07:47] Jordan: Recap in chat with attachments: layer-probe script, canary config, signed model tarball instructions, security checklist, and benchmark.csv template.
[07:56] (end)
